image_description: A large whale is captured mid-action, breaching or slapping its tail against the ocean surface. The whale has a dark, mottled grey body with visible white patches (barnacles/callosities). The tail flukes are raised high out of the water, creating significant splash. The head and anterior body are partially submerged or obscured by the angle and motion.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head is largely submerged or obscured by the angle of the breach and water spray; blowholes are not visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches from barnacles and whale lice.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Visible portions of the body show characteristic mottled grey skin with lighter patches consistent with barnacle colonies.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: No dorsal fin present; multiple dorsal knuckles along posterior back.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the back leading to the tail shows a series of small humps (knuckles) rather than a single prominent dorsal fin, consistent with grey whale anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Robust spindle-shaped body of enormous proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible body mass appears robust and thick, consistent with a large baleen whale.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey with white patches created by barnacles.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail flukes are broad with smooth trailing edge and central notch.
